Desk Clerk

Desk Clerks are student employees who work at our Front Desks, providing customer services and helping our residents feel connected to our University Housing community. Front Desks are open 21-24 hours a day/7 days a week.

Desk Clerk hiring at our Front Desks occurs throughout the year as positions become available with our most significant hiring period taking place in late February/early March in preparation for the following academic year. 

Staff at each Front Desk manage the hiring process for that desk. The staff at the Front Desk(s) you select when you apply for will review your application materials and reach out to you if they are interested in your candidacy if and when there are positions available.           

Desk Clerk

Desk Clerks are student employees who work at our Front Desks, providing customer services and helping our residents feel connected to our University Housing community. Front Desks are open 21-24 hours a day/7 days a week.

Desk Clerk hiring at our Front Desks occurs throughout the year as positions become available with our most significant hiring period taking place in late February/early March in preparation for the following academic year. 

Staff at each Front Desk manage the hiring process for that desk. The staff at the Front Desk(s) you select when you apply for will review your application materials and reach out to you if they are interested in your candidacy if and when there are positions available.                  

Desk Clerks tasks include, but are not limited to: key loans, mail/package processing, recreational and kitchen equipment check out, answering questions, assisting with opening and closing the residence halls, and working with staff who are on call for emergencies.


Dining Office (DCSO) Worker
01/01/2026 to 01/01/2029
Apply Now

Dining Student Office Worker -HFS Office / Cboard 


Dining Office (DCSO) Worker

Dining Student Office Worker -HFS Office / Cboard 


Organizational Relationship:
This position reports to the Assistant Director of Dining Services for Menu Management who is under the supervision the Director of Dining Services. This position is advised by the Assistant Director of Dining Services for Procurement. 

PRIMARY FUNCTION SUMMARY: Under supervision, the position will be trained how to use dining software, how to increase functionality of technology, and participate in process improvement initiatives.  The Dining Technology Student Employee is responsible for complying with all aspects outlined in this Position Description. 

Technology Management (75%)
•    Learn menu management software including, but not limited to, CBORD, NetNutrition, mobile inventory, and FlexCatering. 
•    Uses FlexCatering to manage daily tasks related to a catering operation:
o    Assists in entering nutrition and costing information for new and established recipes
o    Assists in categorizing items and creating systems for report generation
o    Provides assistance and solutions in response to departmental and customer needs
•    Uses CBORD Foodservice Suite (FSS) to manage daily tasks related to a multi-unit foodservice operation:
o    Processes invoices and requisitions
o    Assists in creating standardized system for inventory efficiency
o    Learns, understands, and maintains established naming conventions
o    Maintains FSS ingredient database by correctly entering new items, evaluates for allergens and nutritional content
o    Serves as a resource for any nutritional projects 
o    Participates in and accepts responsibility for departmental projects, as assigned 
o    Provides assistance and solutions in response to departmental and customer needs

Operations (25%)
•    Completes orientation, familiarization with departments, especially within the Dining Services departments, and interrelationships of departments, policies, procedures, individual responsibilities, and routines
•    Maintains established department policies, procedures, objectives, and safety and sanitation standards
•    Maintains harmonious working relationships with department staff and clients
•    Understands and complies with the principles of confidentiality, privileged communications and professional ethics in written and oral communication
•    Participates in educational programs, in-services meetings and periodically attends menu management and production meetings as academic schedule allows
•    Reviews current professional literature to keep abreast of new developments in nutrition and management research and practice
•    Observes management principles in practice, including food production, food procurement, human resource management, and financial management
•    Understands and complies with regulatory agencies

POSITION REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS
•    Strong verbal and written communication skills
•    Strong time management skills 
•    Ability to work independently 
•    Interpersonal skills suitable to working in a complex office and foodservice preparation environment

EDUCATION REQUIRED & PREFERRED:
•    Minimum of 3.0 GPA
•    Current enrollment in the University of Illinois
•    Preferred major in a FSHN or other health-related field, or equally preferred to be enrolled in a Data Science, Computer Science, Informatics or other technology-related field 
•    Preferred to have a current Food Service Manager’s Sanitation Certificate

EXPERIENCE REQUIRED & PREFERRED: 
•    Preferred previous experience working in University Dining or a food service setting

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS and ABILITIES REQUIRED & PREFERRED: 
•    Proficient in Microsoft Office
•    Preferred knowledge of quantity cooking
•    Preferred knowledge of basic menu planning and food preparation

Dining Student Worker

NOW HIRING FOR Fall 2026!  Apply to secure your position for the Fall semester!

Looking for a job that offers a flexible schedule, a fun and welcoming environment, and great food and even better people?  Looking to learn skills that you will utilize for the rest of your life (cooking, teamwork, time management) Join the award-winning University of Illinois Housing Dining team as a Dining Service Worker in one of our 5 dining halls.  Free meals provided!!!

Pay for Dining is $15.50/hr This position is not eligible for benefits.

Graduate Hourly for Residential Experience

The Graduate Hourly for Residential Experience supports the mission of University Housing by contributing to the development, implementation, and assessment of programs and services that enhance the student experience. This position offers hands-on experience in student engagement, administrative operations, and program coordination within a dynamic campus environment. The position description outlines general responsibilities for graduate hourly staff in Residential Life. Specific duties will be provided by the position supervisor, based on the operational needs of their program or area.

Hiring for Graduate Hourly for Residential Experience positions occurs as positions become available.

Residential Life staff who are interested in hiring an Gradaute Hourly will review applications submitted through this portal. These staff members will reach out to you if they are interested in your candidacy if and when there are positions available. Depending on the needs of a particular position, they may ask for additional information and examples of your work. 

Please note: The Graduate Hourly for Residential Experience position is not an assistantship, does not cover tuition costs and does not provide housing. This position is also not a Residence Hall Director role (all of our Residence Hall Directors are full-time Academic Professional staff), nor is it a Resident Advisor role (information about undergraduate RA roles can be found here: recruitment.housing.illinois.edu/undergraduate-resident-advisors; information about graduate/upper-division RA roles can be found here: recruitment.housing.illinois.edu/student/employment/gud-ra).

SDRP Info. Desk and Package Assistant

Application Now Open for the Spring 2027 Semester

Join our University Housing team and help create a welcoming environment rooted in diversity, equity, and inclusion. As a Student Dining & Residential Programs (SDRP) Building Clerk, you will support daily operations by assisting students and visitors at the front desk and helping manage mail services.

Clerks are assigned shifts, typically in 2 to 3 hour increments, during building operating hours, Sunday through Saturday. The SDRP remains open during academic breaks, with hours varying by period.

Pay

  • Building Clerk (Assistant): $15.50 per hour
  • Building Clerk Manager: $16.50 per hour (promotion opportunity available)
  • This position is not eligible for benefits.

Key Responsibilities

Information Desk & Customer Service

  • Serve as the first point of contact for students, staff, and visitors entering the building.
  • Provide accurate information, answer questions, and assist with general inquiries in a professional and welcoming manner.
  • Provide basic technology assistance for Housing events and building operations.

Package Station & Mail Operations

  • Sort, organize, and distribute incoming student mail and packages.
  • Assist students and customers with package pickup and mail-related questions.
  • Help maintain an orderly, efficient, and secure mailroom environment.

Hours & Scheduling

  • Flexible scheduling designed to accommodate academic commitments.
  • Shifts are typically scheduled in 2 to 3 hour increments.
  • Daytime, evening, and weekend shifts are available.
  • The SDRP operates seven days a week, including portions of academic break periods.
  • Employees are expected to work assigned shifts reliably and communicate scheduling conflicts in advance.
  • Weekly hours may vary based on employee availability, operational needs, and staffing levels.

Training & Requirements

  • Must be available to attend mandatory in-person training (dates TBD).

Security Requirements

  • All SDRP Building Clerk positions are designated as security-sensitive positions.
  • A background check may be conducted upon acceptance of a contingent offer.

Student Network Technician (NetTech)

*MUST LIVE IN RESIDENCE HALLS* The student Nework Technician (NetTech) works in residence halls to assist residents with connecting their computers to the hall and campus networks and the Internet. The NetTech assists with associated problems such as virus infections and fulfills an educative function with students by informing them of problem solutions and responsibilities.

Job Description:

  • Communicate to residents' proper use of lab equipment and lab facilities
  • Respond to residents inquiring about malfunctioning hardware or software
  • Identify and report problems with hardware and software on lab computers
  • Ensure that the site environment is conducive to academic work
  • Adhere to schedule of computer and lab maintenance 

This position is not eligible for benefits.
